overview: Montenegro is a small country in the Balkans, on the Adriatic Sea. Its capital is Podgorica. Montenegro was part of Yugoslavia and then of a union with Serbia, until it became independent in 2006. Its name means 'black mountain'. It uses the euro even though it is not a member of the European Union.

geography.text: Montenegro packs a lot into a small space: a sunny Adriatic coastline, including the fjord-like Bay of Kotor, with rugged mountains rising just inland. The north is high and mountainous, with deep canyons such as the Tara River Canyon, one of the deepest in Europe. Lake Skadar, which it shares with Albania, is the largest lake in the Balkans.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Mediterranean on the coast, with cold, snowy winters in the mountains.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Bears and wolves live in the mountains, and Lake Skadar is home to Dalmatian pelicans.

history.text: Montenegro's mountains helped it keep a large degree of independence through centuries of Ottoman power in the Balkans. It was ruled for long periods by prince-bishops and was recognised as independent in 1878. After the First World War it became part of Yugoslavia, and it became independent again after a referendum in 2006.

events.title: Prince-bishops
events.text: The Petrović-Njegoš family begins its long rule.

events.title: Independence recognised
events.text: The Congress of Berlin recognises Montenegro as independent.

events.title: Joins Yugoslavia
events.text: Montenegro becomes part of the new South Slav kingdom.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Montenegrins vote to leave their union with Serbia.

events.title: Joins NATO
events.text: Montenegro becomes a member of NATO.

government.text: Montenegro is a parliamentary republic. Its 81-member parliament chooses the Prime Minister, and the President is elected directly every five years. Montenegro joined NATO in 2017 and is a candidate to join the European Union. It uses the euro, even though it is not in the EU.

economy.text: Tourism on the Adriatic coast is Montenegro's biggest industry. Aluminium, electricity from hydropower and farming are also important. The country is working on new roads to link its coast and mountains.

culture.text: Montenegro's name means 'black mountain'. Its coast is lined with Venetian-era stone towns such as Kotor, set at the end of a deep bay. In the mountains, the old royal capital of Cetinje keeps the country's monasteries and museums.

items.title: Bay of Kotor
items.text: A deep, winding bay with the walled town of Kotor.

items.title: Ostrog Monastery
items.text: A monastery built into a vertical cliff.

items.title: Durmitor
items.text: A national park with a canyon more than 1,000 metres deep.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Njeguški pršut, smoked ham, and cheese from the mountain village of Njeguši.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Folk singing with the gusle, a one-stringed instrument, tells old stories of heroes.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: The Mimosa Festival in Herceg Novi, every February, celebrates the yellow flowers that bloom on the coast.

sport.text: Water polo is Montenegro's most successful sport; the men's team won the European Championship in 2008. Basketball, handball and football are also popular.

items.text: European water polo champions, two years after independence.
Women's handball silver at the London Olympics, Montenegro's first Olympic medal.

didYouKnow: Montenegro uses the euro even though it is not in the European Union.
The Tara River Canyon is one of the deepest in Europe, at about 1,300 metres.

keyPeople.name: Petar II Petrović-Njegoš
keyPeople.text: Wrote The Mountain Wreath, a classic of South Slavic literature.
